title: Throughput sweep and regression detector for HW econ matrix (A10,L4,A100,H100)
creator: Priya Nair
description: Run a controlled throughput sweep across the A10 / L4 / A100 / H100 hardware matrix to produce a canonical tokens/sec and p95 latency report and a repeatable cost-per-token calculation. Build a regression detection rule set (statistical + ML-smoothed) that integrates with the CI/CD alerting pipeline and the Console benchmark dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical benchmark run completed for all four GPUs for seq_len=512 and seq_len=2048 (cold and warm KV cache).
p95 and tokens/sec timeseries stored in datadog with tags: model, hardware, batch_size, seq_len, cache_state, kernel_variant.
Automated regression detector deployed that emits a PagerDuty event when tokens/sec drops >6% for 10+ steady-state minutes or p95 increases >15% vs rolling baseline.
Cost-per-token calculation published to the finance workbook and linked from the Console per-model cost tab.
Benchmark run reproducible from the harness repo with single-command invocation and documented in README.
test_plan: Stage: run synthetic QPS ramps from 0.1x to 3x expected steady QPS to capture tail behavior.
Warmup: 20 minutes steady at target QPS for warm KV/cache measurements.
Cold vs warm: snapshot cold run after VM restart and warm run after 30 minutes of traffic.
Batch sweep: evaluate batch_size in [1,4,8,16] and preferred kernel_variant (fused-attn, cuBLAS path).
Sequence lengths: 512 and 2048 token sequences to surface memory/kv-cache scaling.
Repeat: run each config 3 times to get mean and variance; use median-of-means for regression baseline.
dataset: synthetic prompts derived from product prompt corpus (mix of completion and chat history), seed for randomness saved in repo
metrics_tracked: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (decode token level and request level)
regression_detection_policy: Two-stage detector: (1) Statistical threshold: compare current 10-min rolling median tokens/sec and p95 to 28-day rolling baseline; flag if tokens/sec decline >6% (p=0.01) or p95 increase >15%. (2) ML-smoothed anomaly: EWMA window and seasonal decomposition to mute diurnal noise. Integrate with CI: any detected regression opens a PR against 'benchmarks/regression-log' with attached traces and suggested suspect kernels.
cost_model: Hourly GPU cost (cloud list price) divided by estimated tokens generated per hour from steady-state tokens/sec. Example: if H100 cost = $6.40/hr and measured tokens/sec = 1,200,000 tokens/sec (seq_len=512 profile) => tokens/hr = 4.32B => cost/token = $6.40 / 4.32e9 = 1.48e-9 USD/token. Include amortized infra overhead multiplier (1.15) and network/request overhead (1.05) in final published number.
results_summary: Initial runs show expected ordering in throughput A10 < L4 < A100 < H100 on tokens/sec for seq_len=512. Notable finding: L4 achieves similar tokens/sec to A100 at batch_size 8 for the small model variant due to superior memory bandwidth for small batches; however p95 on L4 had a 20% higher tail under burst profile. Cost-per-token favors L4 for mid-sized workloads (burst-friendly) after overhead multipliers. Detailed CSV results and plots in attachments.
decisions: Publish L4 as a recommended cost-efficient option in Console for mid-range deployments, with an explicit note about higher tail latency under burst traffic.
Add a kernel selection hint in runtime that prefers the fused-attn path on H100/A100 for seq_len>=1024 and batch_size>=8.
Ship regression detector to bench-ci with soft alerts for 2 weeks before escalating to pager duty.
next_steps: Finalize reproducible harness container and add CI job to run nightly smoke sweep (ENG infra team to approve runner quota).
Create Console dashboard card that exposes cost-per-token along with breakouts by kernel_variant and cache_state.
Iterate on regression thresholds after 2 weeks of production telemetry to reduce false positives.
Draft PR to update operations playbook with mitigation steps (rollback to previous kernel variant, increase burst capacity, fallback to cheaper model).
